subject: BrightCorp POC: prompt & log collection, success criteria, and eval timeline
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: BrightCorp POC: prompt & log collection, success criteria, and eval timeline

Hi Anna — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the trial kickoff.

Summary of what we discussed:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference on BrightCorp support triage & suggested-reply use cases (latency and precision for top-1 suggestion).
- Scope: 5K representative prompts + 2 weeks of anonymized chat logs for model conditioning tests + 50 curated eval examples for manual inspection.

Proposed POC success criteria (please confirm / adjust):
1) Latency: median 95th-token latency < 120ms on our dedicated tier for the target prompt length (avg 180 tokens).
2) Precision / business metric: suggested-reply accuracy (top-1 match to your labeled response set) >= 78% on the 50 curated eval cases and no >10% degradation vs your current baseline on the sampled logs.
3) Reliability: <1% error rate (timeouts/errors) over a 48-hour throughput test.

Data handoff & evaluation plan (next actions):
- You: provide sanitized prompt CSV and anonymized chat log NDJSON by Tue 2028-03-21. See required schema below.
- Redwood (Marissa & Vivek): perform ingestion, normalization, and baseline eval within 5 business days of receipt; share results and a short action plan.
- Ownership: BrightCorp data upload (Anna); Redwood ingestion & eval (Marissa); systems/ops validation (Vivek).

Required file formats (to avoid back-and-forth):
- Prompt CSV: columns = prompt_id, prompt_text, channel, avg_tokens_estimate. UTF-8, comma-delimited.
- Chat logs NDJSON: each line = {"session_id","timestamp","speaker","text"}, with PII redacted. If you have multiple channels, provide channel field.

Security / transfer options:
- Preferred: presigned S3 upload that Redwood provides (fast, auditable).
- Alternate: SFTP with access window.
- If you need an NDA addendum or KMS/HSM requirement, flag that and Marissa will loop in Security.

Deliverables & timeline (proposal):
- 2028-03-21: BrightCorp uploads dataset (5K prompts + logs).
- 2028-03-28: Redwood completes baseline ingest and preliminary eval, shares results + short deck.
- 2028-04-04: Joint review call to discuss findings, quality tradeoffs, and rollout plan.

Next steps for this week:
- Anna: confirm upload method (S3 or SFTP) and whether your legal team needs anything else.
- Marissa: I asked her to prepare the ingestion checklist and security contact.

Thanks — I’ll send the presigned S3 instructions once you confirm upload method.

Best,
Michael Grant
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightcorp.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Data Team <data-team@brightcorp.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCorp POC: prompt & log collection, success criteria, and eval timeline

Thanks Michael — appreciate the clear recap. Couple quick items from our side:

1) We'll provide the 5K prompts + two weeks of logs, but we need to sanitize customer identifiers first. Our data team will remove direct PII; will that suffice or do you require a specific hashing scheme?
2) Preferred transfer: presigned S3 is good for us. We'll need the bucket name and an upload window of ~72 hours.
3) Attachments: attaching a small sample (first 200 prompts + 2 days of chat NDJSON) so you can validate schema.

Attachments (sample):
- brightcorp_prompts_20280314.csv (csv, 200 rows)
- chat_logs_anon_20280314.ndjson (ndjson, 2 days)

Questions:
- On success metric #2 (78% top-1 accuracy) — is that on exact-match to your model’s response or fuzzy similarity? We need to understand how Redwood measures match vs our human labels.
- On the 5 business day baseline: does that include tuning runs (e.g., temperature/batch) or is it just a straight out-of-the-box evaluation?

We aim to upload full dataset by Mon 2028-03-20 if that works.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Liu
Head of Product, BrightCorp
anna.liu@brightcorp.com | +1 (212) 444-9922
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCorp POC: prompt & log collection, success criteria, and eval timeline

On Wed, Mar 14, 2028 at 5:03 PM, Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightcorp.com> wrote:
> Thanks Michael — appreciate the clear recap. Couple quick items from our side:
> ...

Anna — great questions. Quick answers and clarifications below:

- PII / hashing: redaction is fine. If you can replace email/IDs with stable hashed ids (sha256 truncated) that helps us map sessions to labels without re-identifying users. If hashing is hard, full redaction (replacing with <REDACTED>) is acceptable but please keep session_id stable across events. Marissa will share a short sanitization checklist.

- Presigned S3: we will send a presigned PUT URL + bucket path once you confirm upload target. 72-hour window is fine. If you prefer, we can also issue a temporary role (short-lived credentials) — let me know.

- Matching metric clarifications: our initial eval uses a normalized token-overlap + fuzzy similarity (normalized edit distance + embedding cosine) to compute a match score; for the POC we will report both exact-match and fuzzy-match percentages so you can pick the threshold that maps to your business metric. The 78% was a suggested target on fuzzy-match; we can break down results for exact vs fuzzy in the report.

- Baseline runs: the 5 business-day window covers ingestion, normalization, and a baseline set of runs with 2 tuned settings (default + customer-tuned temperature/batch). Extensive hyperparameter optimization is outside the baseline scope but we can schedule a follow-up if you want a tuning pass.

Action items we’ll take on:
- Marissa: finalize sanitization checklist and security contact info (expected today).
- Vivek: will prepare a lightweight normalization script (Python) to align your prompt formats with our eval harness. He will also be the point for any runtime-specific notes.
- Michael: will generate presigned S3 instructions & upload path (ETA today).

We’ll plan to kick off ingestion once you upload. Thanks again — we’re excited to get started.

Best,
Michael
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brightcorp.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-16T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCorp POC: prompt & log collection, success criteria, and eval timeline

Anna / Michael — quick note from the engineering side. Thanks for the sample files; I ran a quick pass and left inline comments in the shared Drive doc (link above). Two practical items: 

1) I’ll deliver a normalization script (Python, ~150 LOC) that: trims signatures, collapses repeated whitespace, and maps your channel field into our eval channels. I’ll upload it to the Drive folder.
2) Timeline: once we have the full dataset, Redwood will complete an initial baseline eval (ingest + default + one tuned config) within 5 business days and post results to the Drive. If we hit any schema issues I’ll raise them directly in the doc.

If you’re comfortable, confirm S3 and we’ll send the presigned upload link today.

Thanks — Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
